content.title: Official Blind Review #1
content.review:
This paper proposes an alternative to Squeeze and Excitation (SE) Block to learn a gating function that re-scales a feature tensor which is passed as input to it. On the positive side, there are certainly differences in the design between this paper and SE, and the proposed block seems to be more lightweight than SE (although the cost for employing SE is tiny) .Moreover, the authors present a large number of experiments by applying their block to several different problems and architectures. 

However, on the negative side, I feel that the contribution is too incremental for ICLR, since the proposed block seems like more like a heavy engineered extension of SE. Moreover, comparison with SE is missing from many experiments. It is absolutely critical that SE numbers appear in all reported results.

content.title: Response to Reviewer #1
content.comment:
We appreciate you taking the time to share your comments in the review assessment. Your comments are addressed point by point as follows.

We would like to first highlight the following differences to Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) Networks. 
1) SE-Nets leverage channel attention for channel relationship modeling, while our proposed GCT is motivated by the typical normalization methods (e.g.,  Local Response Normalization [1]). Compared to the fully-connected layers used by SE, these normalization methods can naturally create competition between different channels while taking much fewer parameters and computational resources. 2) SE-Nets implicitly model channel relationships with a fully-connected (FC) operation, while we designed explainable control parameters to make our GCT more efficient and easier to analyze. The embedding weights $\alpha$ are responsible for controlling the weight of each channel, and the gating weights $\gamma$ and bias $\beta$ are designed to adjust the output of the gate channel-wisely.

In our paper, we visualize the GCT parameters in Fig. 3. It clearly shows that the network prefers to create channel competition in shallow layers. On the contrary, it creates channel cooperation in deep layers.

Though you felt our approach is incremental to SE-Nets, we think the aforementioned technical contributions are not trivial.
GE [2] is an extension method of SE. This paper was accepted in NeurIPS 2018. In GE, they modified SE by pooling information locally instead of globally. GE performs better but introduces more parameters and computational complexity.
In our paper, we introduced a new direction to improve SE-like architectures. Our GCT is not just a simple extension. Intuitively, we demonstrate that the performance can be improved with a more general transformation method. It is more light-weight and explainable to augment the network with our GCT. Our introduced control variables can be leveraged to further analyze the behavior of the network. Remarkably, compared to SE, we achieve better accuracy with less computational cost on ImageNet.
We hope future research studies will be encouraged to improve SE-Nets, better analyze the component, and understand channel relationships clearer.

We are very welcome to all criticisms. Meanwhile, we sincerely hope the comments can be more detailed in order to avoid confusion. We would appreciate your kindness if you could provide more specific feedback to improve our paper. Thank you in advance.

Our responses to the other comments are below:

Q1: The proposed block seems to be more lightweight than SE (although the cost for employing SE is tiny).
A1: Thank you for recognizing that our block is more light-weight. Note that when we apply SE-like blocks to more convolutional layers, the cost will become more significant. In the original SE-Nets paper, SE modules were applied in block-level, such as a Res-Block or an Inception-Block. However, to benefit from the channel attention in the whole network, a more general method is to apply SE to every convolutional layer. However, the cost of employing SE for every convolutional layer is quite heavy (Table 6). The SE counterpart increases the network inference cost by 70%. Our GCT only increases 16% of the cost and achieves a better performance.

Q2: Comparison with SE is missing from many experiments.
A2: We followed GE to compare our GCT with SE on the popular ImageNet classification benchmark fairly. In addition, we made our comparison on more modern networks, including residual and non-residual. Under the condition of comparable GFLOPs, GCT outperforms SE in the backbones of ResNet-50, ResNeXt-50, and Inception-v3, while GCT uses much fewer parameters. Under the condition of using the same number of SE or GCT, our GCT outperforms SE in accuracy, GFLOPs and parameter amount. All these results are shown in Table 2.


[1] Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey E Hinton. Imagenet classification with deep convolutional neural networks. In NIPS, 2012. 
[2] Jie Hu, Li Shen, Samuel Albanie, Gang Sun, and Andrea Vedaldi. Gather-excite: Exploiting feature context in convolutional neural networks. In NIPS, 2018.

content.title: Official Blind Review #3
content.review_assessment:_checking_correctness_: I assessed the sensibility of the derivations and theory.
content.review:
The authors propose Gated Channel Transformation (GCT) for efficient and accurate contextual information modeling for CNN. They introduce using l2 normalization instead of FC-layers (and instead of batch norm, etc.) and they introduce channel-wise parameters for controlling the behavior of the gated adaptation of feature channels. These three parameters (gating weights and biases to control the activation of the gate; embedding weights) per channel.

The performance is measured in three different experiments on standard datasets (some of them a bit old, however, sufficient); One can see a significant performance increase of the proposed method using various architectures even though the method uses less trainable parameters.

All in all, the paper reads well and gives sufficient information about the parameters and experimental details used. I just think that the possible reader group would not be so big. It would be great if the code would also be publisehd, and maybe that the whole experiments could be made purely reproducible.

The paper has a long list of references. I think that some could even be removed (e.g., sometimes you list 4 rreferences for a single statement); furthermore, it is enough to add the citation only once (especially when being in the same sentence).

It is advised to avoid abbreviations which are very commonly used for different methods in common literature (e.g., GA would be genetic algorithm).

content.title: Response to Reviewer #3
content.comment:
We appreciate you taking the time to share your comments in the review assessment.

Besides, thank you for that you pointed out the inadequacies of our submission. We have removed unnecessary references and ambiguous abbreviations.

Finally, we are delighted that you recognize our work, and the code of the GCT module implemented by using PyTorch is below here:

======================================================
class GCT(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_channels, epsilon=1e-5):
        super(GCT, self).__init__()
        self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(1, in_channels, 1, 1))
        self.gamma = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, in_channels, 1, 1))
        self.beta = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, in_channels, 1, 1))
        self.in_channels = in_channels
        self.epsilon = epsilon

    def forward(self, x):
        s = (x.pow(2).sum((2,3), keepdim=True) + self.epsilon).pow(0.5) * self.alpha
        a = self.gamma / (s.pow(2).mean(dim=1, keepdim=True) + self.epsilon).pow(0.5)
        s_ = 1. + torch.tanh(s * a + self.beta)
        return x * s_
======================================================

content.title: Official Blind Review #2
content.review:
The core of the paper is around a block to gate cnn outputs between layers controlled by a global context. The outputs of the block are combined with the original cnn outputs via a residual connection.

None of the ideas is particularly new, but the main contribution seems to be to show that we can still get benefits in various tasks by using a very simple setup with l2 global norm per channel for the global pooling context scaled by simple linear transformations per cnn output channel + tanh activation for the gating function. By itself I think this is a good practical finding and good tinkering results should always be welcomed in my opinion.

However, had the paper been more succinct, with less attempts at interpretation and without trying to present a fundamentally new unit (we have too many acronyms already), I'd be more open to accept it. Sentences like "This capability is more consistent with the training process in biological neural networks..." in section 3  and various attempts at interpretation (as the whole section 4.4) come across as a little pretentious and only obfuscate the main finding in my opinion. 

The experiments are pretty extensive, and I believe just studying the effects of adding global pooling contexts between the layers on the various tasks is interesting by itself.

Some minor comments on presentation:

Figure 1: It would be clearer not to include the residual connection inside the building block (i.e., just tanh and not (1+ tanh). Same for "Gating Adaptation" on Section 3. I would just highlight that the proposed gating block is combined with the original output with residual connections.

A short segment of code (as reviewer #3 points out) would make it immediately obvious what is being proposed and highlight the simplicity of it.

Conclusion and Future Work: "We conduct expensive" -> "We conduct extensive" ?

Appendix. Experiments on CIFAR seem unnecessary at this point, and I don't think the visualizations (and accompanying interpretations) add much to the paper.
